utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, would you call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We call Dragan Petrovic. DRAGAN PETROVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that is being handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell the Court your name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Dragan Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where do you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you been engaged by the Defence as an investigator in the case of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you been working with the Defence on location in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to present Defence Exhibit D55 to the witness, please. (Handed). Sir, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Who made that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where did you make that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: At a specific place in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in front of one of the houses in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to show to the witness a map for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be Defence 97. The Prosecution has a copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you recognise that map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you tell us what map it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the map of part of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you identify the triangle on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to tender this map.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Defence 97?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: For the convenience of the Bench, I have three additional copies. Sir, I will ask you to put the map on the overhead projector and the usher may assist you in that matter. I think we need a larger view, yes, the whole map, if possible, a larger view of the map. Could it be enlarged? That is how it is. Mr. Petrovic, could you point out the triangle on the map for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the triangle right here. [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: There is a pointer on your desk, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not see one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you point out the triangle again and hold it still for just a few seconds?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court where this photograph has been taken from, from which point on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you describe that point to the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the photo was taken in front of the one of the houses in Kozarac -- actually it was the pastry shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to show a photograph to the witness for identification, please. Can you tell us what you see on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is you, Mr. Wladimiroff, in front of the pastry shop from where the photograph has been taken from.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender that photograph. I have extra copies for the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am trying to get the transcript on my monitor. It is not coming up on Judge Stephen's. It is not coming up on any of our screens. There we are. OK. No objection to Defence 98. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is it right that your photographs which were compiled into Exhibit D55 have been taken from the point where the person on this photograph is standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If you look on the photograph, the large photograph, the compilation again, and if you also look on the map, can you show on the map what we see on that large photograph? Could you use the pointer again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Start on your left hand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: OK. We see the house here on the left side, on the corner.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me Mr. Wladimiroff, that 55 -----

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Enlargement.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. I am having difficulty following it. I suppose you have the Court's copy of 55?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We gave the Bench ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sorry, Judge Vohrah has it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, I am sorry. You can go back then and tell us about 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Petrovic, would you be so kind as to show on the map again with the pointer starting with your left hand what we see on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We see the house on the left side here, on the map, on the right side we see the corner here where some bushes are in front of the school and the triangle, the square, in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you lower the map just a bit ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Just before that, would you be able to get the witness to point out from where this photograph is taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. You mean the small photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Mr. Petrovic, can you point out again on the map where the small photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated] From somewhere around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please be so kind as to lower the map a little bit on the overhead projector, just a bit? Thank you. Can you point on the map to us where the school is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you run a test on that triangle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Court what was the test about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The test was about whether it was possible to see somebody walking across the street by the triangle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I am going to show a photograph to the witness for identification, your Honour. As a matter of fact, I may show him three photographs in order to speed things up. I suggest that you mark them A, B and C. Do you recognise these photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Before we go into these photographs, can you show on the map what actually happened during that test?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do it slowly with your pointer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure. You walked from here, from this gate that you can see on the photograph, across past the triangle and stopped here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was still at the same position in front of the pastry shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you take photographs of my movements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Are these the photographs in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I tender these photographs, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 99A, B and C?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have extra copies for the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness could point out the pastry shop again on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I will, your Honour. Perhaps, witness, I can ask you to mark on the map in front of you the pastry shop with a pen that will be given to you by the usher or a marker. I think that is a better idea indeed. The Prosecution has a marker that is appropriate to mark the pastry shop in green. Thank you. I will give you a yellow marker. Could you mark on the map where I walked, where I started and where I ended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is where you started.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Draw the whole line. Thank you. If we look to the first photograph, can you describe what the photograph shows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It shows you starting -- when you started your walk from the gate and stopped at the triangle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you took the photograph while I stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What does the next photograph show?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next photograph shows that when you were standing right on the triangle, on the point of the triangle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did I walk or did I stop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You stopped again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What does the last photograph show?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is where you ended the process, where you stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court on each photograph by putting the photograph on the overhead projector where is the first thing you photographed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: OK. Can I take the map down?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we could enlarge it a bit. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put the next photograph on the overhead projector?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you, and the last one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. When were these photographs taken, made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In which month of the year were these photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: August.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If you would be so kind as to put the map on the overhead projector again, a little bit more upwards, higher?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does not go any higher than this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: All right. Can you show on the map where the church is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you inspect the neighbourhood of that church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What did you inspect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To see whether there were lamp posts, whether there were posts or poles at the church, in front of the church or on the road by the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you point on that map where you saw poles? Perhaps we can ask you to mark it with a pink marker? If we can ask the usher to assist you again to have this map completely on the overhead projector so we can see what you have marked. Thank you. Your Honour, I am going to show photos for identification to the witness, and may they be marked as A and later on I will show B and C.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is Defence 100A, B and C, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you see poles on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you see a pole in front of a house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you put that photograph on the overhead projector, please, on top of the map? Can you point to that pole in front of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender that photograph, your Honour, as 100A.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 100A will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you show on the map the place of the pole you just pointed out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put the photograph on the overhead projector again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes. Do you see any lamp post on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you see a lamp post on the other pole more in front of that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you point that out, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have copies for the Bench. If I now may present the next photograph ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I am sorry, but could you also get the witness to show where this photograph 100 was taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, I certainly will. Witness, you have heard the question. Could you answer it, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you want to know the position from where it was taken or?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: On the map, from where it was taken.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: In which direction?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you point out not only where you were standing but -- right, the direction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From here towards the lamp post.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I am going to show you another photograph -- 100B, that will be -- for identification. Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you see a pole on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you put that photograph on the overhead projector, please -- a little bit more to the right so we see the map? Thank you very much. Can you point to that pole, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I tender this photograph, your Honour, as 100B?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 100B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you notice any lamp or lamp post on that pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If you go back to the previous photograph and put that one on the overhead projector too, we see in front of that house two poles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you describe the difference between those poles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the old pole and this is the new pole.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put back on the overhead projector 100B, please? Thank you. What kind of a pole is that, an old one or a new one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is there an old one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What do we see, the old one or the new one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We can see both.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. If you go to the map, can you point out on the map what we see? Which pole on the map do we see here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you point out from which point that photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you point out the direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. I am going to show a third photograph, your Honour. Did I give the Bench photographs of the church?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Then I will give you those photographs too.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, could you point out to me on 100B the second pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I see one but ......

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: It is a little bit difficult.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I see, behind it. OK. That is the old pole ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- behind it? OK. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Witness, could you look at the third photograph that has been given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What do you see on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see two poles on that photograph taken in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: An old one and a new one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you put that photograph on the overhead projector, please? Can you point out to us these poles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is the old one and this is the new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. I tender that photograph as 100C, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 100C will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have three photographs for the Bench again. [To the witness]: Can you point on the map which poles we see here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you point out from which point the photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Adding the direction of -- yes. Thank you. Do you see a lamp post or a lamp on this last photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you see one on the old one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Perhaps you would take the photograph from the overhead projector in your hands and inspect the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. On the old one. If you want, I can point out where.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. If we go back to the map again, we see three poles marked on your map, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If I start on the pole that is south of the church, could you point to that pole, please, for us on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean this one here?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: South of the church. Right. Does that pole have a lamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Go to the next pole. Does that pole or one of the poles over there have a lamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Go to the next pole. Does that pole, one of the poles over there, have a lamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. While being there taking these photographs and inspecting the poles, did you speak to the priest who was living on the compound of the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you discuss with the priest the lamps and the poles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you ask the priest whether there was a lamp on the pole in the mid of the three poles in front of the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I was waiting until the finish of the question and the answer, but then I am going to object if he is going to testify for the priest, your Honour, as hearsay which is not directly relevant to .....

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, your Honour, according to your ruling, we found that we were allowed to go this far.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We look for indicia of reliability, of course, and we admit any relevant evidence that has probative value. Some hearsay may have probative value as long as there is some indicia of reliability. I suppose he is a priest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That was raised in ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: It is also my understanding that this was one of the witnesses on the witness list who refused to come and testify themselves, so I think that does raise an issue of the reliability of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will overrule the objection, Mr. Keegan. We will hear it. As we have indicated, our rules allow us to hear evidence. If we determine that it lacks the probative value, then we can exclude it. The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Petrovic, you may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, can you repeat the question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: The question was whether you discussed with the priest living on the compound near the church the poles and the lamps standing in front of the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did discuss it with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you ask him whether there was a lamp on that pole or one of the poles in front of the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you ask whether there was a lamp from early 1992 on that pole ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: --- of those poles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where there lamps on those poles, according to what has been told to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Which ones are they now, Mr. Wladimiroff, which poles?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is the pole in front of the church, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: There is no lamp on 100B, is that correct, from what we can see?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That was evidence that was given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then there was no lamp also in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is what has been told by the witness, your Honour. That is all I ask, your Honour. Did I tender C?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If I have not, I ask you to allow me to tender it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to 100C?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS FEATHERSTONE
utterances.text: It is in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: All right. That is all I ask, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you said that you did this test on the square in August 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Were you ever in Kozarac during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So you have no idea what the condition of the square is and the shrubbery around the square during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what type of camera and lens you used to take these photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was one of those automatic cameras which has a zoom lens.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know what setting the lens was on when you took these photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember but I know that the lens was on. It was used. I really do not remember at what level or whatever you call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So you cannot testify to this Court what effect the setting of the lens may have had on the perception of distance as it appears in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know for a fact that the lens was used, zoom lens, a small one, which one of those automatic cameras have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you yourself gain custody of this map of Kozarac that has been tendered, Defence 97?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where did you get it from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Mr. Wladimiroff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know when or where he got it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you have any idea of the scale of this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So you can’t tell us the approximate distance from the location where you took the photograph to the distance across the square?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could because I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you measure it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. The Defence Exhibit 100, do you still have those three photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Sorry, which one are we talking about, the square or the church?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, I am sorry, this is the church light poles, Defence Exhibit 100. Defence Exhibit 100C is the photograph which was taken closest to the centre of town. That is just the picture of the two poles.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. From looking at the plan of the map and where you approximately drew that light pole, there are no buildings immediately adjacent to those light poles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there is just the priest house behind the lamp poles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: On the other side of those trees that we see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. Looking at that photograph, it is apparent that the electrical wires are all connected to the old pole, the wooden pole, not to the new pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If we look at the picture of 100A which is the other end, the photograph where you have the light poles and the house showing, the roof of the house showing ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: --- it appears that the electrical wires, in fact, have now been connected to the new pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: But there is still, apparently, a light fixture attached to the old pole, although there are no wires going to that pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When we look at the church picture, which is 100B, it appears that the old pole is leaning over, having fallen over, and all the wires have been connected to the new pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In fact, it is actually a junction for the wires coming from the two different directions on the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: But no light has been attached to the new pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you were asking the priest, did you ask him when there was a light on that old pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Which war is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The war in 1992, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If I may have just a moment, your Honour? Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, would you be so kind as to put the map again on the overhead? It is still there, if we have the overhead projector on? If we could have the map brought down, please, so we see the triangle on it? Could you put your pointer on the pastry shop where you have marked it? Right. Could you run your pointer to the yellow line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is the distance between the pastry shop and that line, according to your experience of having been there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 10 to 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing, your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: This is much the best map we have had so far in detail, Mr. Wladimiroff. Would the witness be able to point out, first of all, the first aid centre?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Witness, are you able to point out on this map the first aid centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Does that mean the first aid centre in the school?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: No, I mean sometimes called the hospital.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Can you point out the Tadic home and cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Would you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Am I right in thinking that the post office and picture theatre are off this map, further up the Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What is the big building with "3536" on it which is on the corner facing the triangle?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: "3536", it is numbered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is part of the school.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: That is part of the school as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes. Then the building, two buildings, up Marsala Tita Street from 3536 on the same side of the road, is that the restaurant? It has three little projections towards Marsala Tita Street on that frontage.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next to the 3537?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Next to 3537, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure whether it is a restaurant. It looks like a shop to me, some sort of a shop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Witness, if you look at the spread picture, can you tell me where the school is? Can you point out where the school is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, shall I put it on the overhead projector?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated] This is the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, regarding 100B, which is the church you indicated where you took that photograph from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: That would have been across the street from the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Some distance up from the church or directly across the church, from the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is across on the road.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: How many feet were you from the church when you took the photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not very far. I do not know measurements in feet. I was a few metres away.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you see any kind of a plum orchard where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Plum orchard?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do not ask me to explain!

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were you on the road or were you next to whatever growth, if there was any growth, there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry? I am sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Where were you when you took the photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was on the road. I was on the road all the time when these three photos were taken.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: OK. That would have been at how many feet or metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five to 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Five to 10 metres. OK. Do you know when the new poles went up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Do you know, what was the condition of the old poles when the new poles were not there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, what the priest has told me is that they did not have lights for a very, very long time there.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: That is in B, 100B?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What about 100C, there is a light on the old pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same thing.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So the lights were there, but they just were not operative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour, nothing arises.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the long D55 and the new Exhibit D99, those were both taken on the same day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you take both of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Tell me, if you put these two photographs one on top of the other ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: --- can you explain to me why it appears that the group of people who are in the triangle appear much to be farther away in D99 than they do in D55? Did you change the lens setting between taking those photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possibly, I cannot recall. But this also has -- just one moment, please. Possibly, but this photocopy looks to be a little bit enlarged, just a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: May I ask you this: when you took the photograph of the poles at the church which is D100B, do you recall what was behind you when you took that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which one was that, D100?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, that is the photo of the church. Do you recall what was behind you when you took that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Trees, house, bushes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Trees, houses and bushes. OK. Did you ask the priest his name, this priest that you spoke to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Out of an abundance of caution, your Honour, could we have this paper given to the witness and could you write down the name for us, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, no protection has been asked.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I was thinking the same. I thought that Mr. Tadic had -----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I could not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: There is no problem. MR. KEEGAN (To the witness): Can you tell us the priest's name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mladen Majkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Nothing arises, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. Petrovic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, you are free to leave. You are permanently excused. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you call the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next witness is Mr. Thomas Deichmann. MR. THOMAS JEURGEN DEICHMANN, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is he the witness listed as 38 or 39?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not have the list in front of me, but I believe so, as media expert.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that is being given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could you give the Court your full name please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thomas Jeurgen Deichmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How old are you, Mr. Deichmann?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 33 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are of German nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You live in Frankfurt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is your occupation at the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Frankfurt?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Eppsteiner Strasse 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have given your address. I asked for your occupation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is all right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What is occupation?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is your job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My job is I am a journalist -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is all right. If you can tell us, first of all, what your reason for being called by the Defence to give evidence in this case is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was asked by Mr. Wladimiroff to look at the German media, and mainly how often they reported about the Tadic case since his arrest in February 1994, and mainly concentrate about the question how often he was shown with photos in TV. That was a main thing I looked at. But I also did some research on important printed media, like newspapers or journals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did your study also take into account British newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did a brief study with British newspapers as well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps you can tell us a little bit about your background, what employments and what your jobs have been, perhaps since 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right. I studied civil engineering with a diploma. I finished in '89. I worked as a civil engineer at Technical University in Darmstadt for a couple of months, and in 1990 I started working for a publishing house in Frankfurt for a year. Afterwards, in 1991, I did work again as a civil engineer in an office, civil engineering office, close to Frankfurt. At the beginning of 1993 I only did work as a journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Since 1994 have you worked for the London International Research Exchange?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What has been the feature of your employment with that Exchange?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we concentrate on different, special topics and mainly look at how the media report on these topics. So the first major project we did was about D Day. So we looked at how different papers in Britain, Germany -- I looked at the coverage in Germany -- reported about D day. We even did a very good report about this called "History as News" which was published in Britain. The second project was images of Japan which is nearly finished called "Images of Japan" where we looked at the media coverage about Japan in the new period in relation to the 50th anniversary of bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. The final report (which will be published as well) is due to be finished in a couple of months, I hope. The third project we only just started, that we had a launching meeting in London a couple of months ago, it is called "Journalists at War", media coverage after post cold war conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You yourself, as a journalist and author, have you written for a number of different publications within Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, altogether since 1993 about 30 different papers in Europe, not only in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Has also material written by you been cited upon television programmes within Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have been invited to some programmes on the stuff I was writing. I have also been invited to some conferences, or to some, as an expert talking about the media, for example, how they responded to censorship in the Internet at the beginning of this year, or that the journalism school in Cologne, Institut Fuer Publizistik. I did a brief introduction there and so, and to radio stations as well I have been invited to talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have developed contacts with a wide variety of news stations and newspapers within Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And also within other countries in Europe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. So I could name a couple, if that is of interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Germany, the biggest paper I was writing for was Die Woche, a weekly paper, but I have also been writing for newspapers like Hanoverische Zeitung, Die Welt, Die Tageszeitung. In Europe, I have been writing for the Wiener Standard or the Grune Amsterdamer, Helsingbor Dagblad in Sweden -- so quite a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were instructed by the Defence to look at the media coverage within Germany concerning the arrest and processing of Dusko Tadic through the criminal justice system of Germany as well as his appearance for trial at The Hague, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Has your background, expertise and experience been something that you have been able to apply to this task?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, of course, because I covered the war quite extensively the last couple of years and I already had a big archive and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was going to ask you about that. Had you also been able to have access to materials that had already been prepared by you, to look at various features of the conflict within the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. So, what I just said, I did my own archive in the last three or four years where I covered actually three or four daily papers and weekly papers as well and I collected everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you prepared a report for the Defence which sets out, in fact, the matters that you were asked to consider, as well as the products of your research in relation to a selected number of television stations within Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In addition to that, newspapers and magazines within Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As well information provided to you by others who had also done research on this matter and with whom you had contact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a report that contains a number of facts, figures and details. The Prosecution have been served with a copy. It will be information more easily digestible by the Court if the report is given to you rather than having to listen to it and absorb it, purely from the oral testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He is going to testify about the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Testify about what is contained in the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There are various appendices that provide the information within the report.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Just one second, your Honour, we have lost the transcript again.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 101.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 101. If we give it the suffix (A) and there are three copies here for the Bench. Mr. Deichmann has his own copy and the Prosecution has theirs already.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit 101A ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Deichmann, is it correct that the Tadic case was viewed with great interest within the German media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Not least because of the history of that country and the atmosphere after 50 years of the war ending and internal debates within Germany concerning events within the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I think that is an important point or important points to bear in mind. First of all, that in Germany everything that is linked with the Nazi past, German Nazi past, is always of big interest for the media and also for the public, for politicians, and the Tadic case was very often linked with the German past. So, for example, he was imprisoned in February 1994 in Munich and he was supposed to be complicit to genocide -- is that the right word?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So the term "genocide" was quite often in the public. There were comparisons or articles mentioning and also TV programmes that he was working in a concentration camp, so there was a clear link. Also, that the work of the Tribunal itself was of a very big interest for the German media also because they made comparisons with the Nuremberg trials after the Second World War. I think one point which maybe made it even more interesting than in a normal period was that all these anniversaries, 50th anniversaries, of the end of the Second World War were expected to be celebrated, not only in Germany, so there was actually more interest in this whole subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. From your research, if I just summarise it this way, at the start of your evidence, would it be right to say, from your experience and coverage of the media at that time in 1994 and from your research, that you were able to determine that pictures of Dusko Tadic had been shown regularly on German TV ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- and pictures were regularly put in newspapers and magazines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Also of interest within German society was the proximity of Germany and the European Community to Yugoslavia itself and Yugoslavia being considered as part of Europe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think that is another important point to bear in mind why the media were very interested in the case. It was German politics was very involved, like the European countries, in the conflict and also it was Tadic, he was imprisoned in Germany. So it was the first case which was, I think, worldwide reported quite regularly about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A third feature which would have been of interest within German society was a number of agencies, non-governmental organisations such as the Society for Threatened People, who had roots and links and contacts within Germany and had bases within that country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did quite a lot of campaigning around the Tribunal work and, for example, at the first hearing in November 1994 they even did a protest outside the building here and their boss, Mr. Tilman Zuelch, was in TV very regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A number of prominent German public figures who are in control of these organisations or the directors are, in fact, people who frequently have access to the media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, quite frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have set out in your report a number of such organisations and what their influence is. I would like to now turn to matters concerning television programmes. If you can perhaps deal with, first of all, the TV stations that you are aware of and their market share based on viewing figures? If you could perhaps give those details to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right. The market shares are from August 1996 and the biggest journal is RTL which is a private channel with 16.8 per cent market shares. The second one is ARD, Erstes Deutsches Fernsehen, the first programme which is not private. It is 14.6 per cent market shares. The third one is ZDF, the second German television station, not private as well, with 13.8 per cent market shares. The fourth is a private journal again, Sat1, Sat Ein, with 13.5 per cent. Then ARD, the third programmes, which are regional programmes belonging to the first programme in Germany. They have got 10.3 per cent market shares. Then No. 6 is Pro7, a private channel again, with 9.0 per cent and RTL2 is No. 7 with 4.2 per cent. I only listed n-TV as a private news channel with only 0.3 per cent because I have some more information about this later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So, in fact, the three dominant stations are RTL, ARD and ZDF in that order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that order, yes, and if you look at news programmes, in particular, it is a little bit changed. The order No. 1 is ARD, No.2 is ZDF and No. 3 is RTL.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Taking, first of all, then ARD which you have said is the most important of the stations for news coverage, were you through your contacts at that television station provided with information from their computer concerning the period between November 1994 and May 1996 and the reports about the Tadic case on the main news programmes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they provided me with a list which explained that in their main programmes, which is Tagesschau at 8 p.m., Tagesthemen at 10.30 p.m., and then a weekly magazine, Wochenspiegel, they had 11 reports about the Tadic case, and at least eight of them used photos of Tadic. That is altogether, and I could split it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, is that information provided in the form of a computer printout that came from that television station ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- which has been labelled for your report as appendix 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, again a copy of this has been provided to the Prosecution and I put it before the Court as 101B.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 101B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There are three copies for your Lordships. [To the witness]: Have you actually been through the material that was produced in computer printout form by that television station and which has been labelled appendix 1, our Exhibit 101B?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This information was provided from the archives of the television station, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They provide a service whereby references, key words as well as photographic images, can be traced through their system and, in fact, produced in a computer printout form?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is actually what every TV channel or a newspaper can do these days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you could tell us then what you were able to analyse from ARD and the news programmes of that television station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right. So, if you split these reports up in the main news items which is Tagesschau shown at 8 p.m., there were three reports in Tagesschau at different days about the Tadic case, the first in November 1994, in April 1995 and in May 1996 and in all of them they showed photos of Tadic. Additional information which I got from another source is that in the average 8.19 million people watched the Tagesschau at 8 o'clock and there are additional Tagesschau news reports, shorter ones, during daytime at 2 p.m., 3 p.m., 4 p.m., 5 p.m., even in the morning as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the figure that you have just given us about the three reports for the main daily news programme of ARD at 8 p.m. is merely for that programme at 8 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it then also the case that the other daily slots for the Tagesschau recycle the news throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very often, but I do not have really material on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: These programmes to which you have referred, were they solely about the defendant Dusko Tadic or were they also dealing with wider issues but also contained references to Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I would have to look at it again in more detail but, in general, Tadic was mentioned at least, he was shown with a photo. But some of them took it in a broader context, so there were reports about the work of the Tribunal and then very often in such a report Tadic was mentioned or shown with a photo. But it was not all of them, so I did not look at it in this case, purely on Tadic, on the Tadic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In fact, in the evidence that you are about to give that is often the case; some programmes specifically upon the defendant Dusko Tadic, but other programmes dealing with general subjects such as the Tribunal or attempts to arrest Dr. Karadzic, but there would be at some stage a focus upon Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could you also tell us about the other daily show containing the day's news at 10.30 p.m. on ARD?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is Tagesthemen at 10.30 and they had six reports about the Tadic case, as we just discussed it briefly with the Tagesschau, and five of them showed photos of Tadic, so one without a photo, and these five were broadcasted in February 1994 on 13th and 14th, so twice in February 1994, that was shortly after his arrest. Then the next one in November 1994. That was after the first hearing. Then April 1995, that was a period when Tadic was deferred to the Tribunal, and again in May 1996 when the hearings at the Tribunal again had a very big coverage and that also is, in general, just a brief comment also at the times when, in general, the media were very interested in the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As is the case with the Tagesschau at 8 p.m., is there also a nightly news programme called Nachtmagazin where the material from those other main news programmes is recycled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is true as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would that be right to describe that as a sort of round-up of the day's news?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is relayed, I think, at 0.30 in the morning and at 2 o'clock or so in the morning again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can now turn to the second most prominent German television station in terms of news features, and that is ZDF, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you speak to someone at ZDF in relation to the matter for which you had been instructed by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did they, in fact, not provide any computer information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They were not able to provide this kind of information on computer printout.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But did they, in fact, check their computer system and give you the information that they had within it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They did a check on the computer in the archive and they found 18 reports where Tadic at least was mentioned, but they could not give me any information how many photos were used. It was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This was between February 1994 and October 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The 18 reports were within the two main news programmes Heute and Heute Journal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the equivalent to Tagesschau and Tagesthemen in the first programme ARD. Heute is at 8 p.m. watched by 5.34 million people or households and also repeated during day time a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the other one is Heute Journal watched by 3.55 million people or households broadcasted once a day only at 9.45 p.m. Then there was also like in our day during night time Heute Nacht, another news programme, which very often repeated what has been broadcasted already during day time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: These periods where we are looking at the use of the name of Dusko Tadic and his photographic image for the television stations, were they at periods when it was a major story within Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We are not dealing here with an obscure piece of news given a low ranking; this was news given the highest ranking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, especially in the periods I just outlined after his arrest in Munich ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- I would say that was the most important period. Then after the first hearing in November '94 at the Tribunal, then when he was deferred in April/May 1995, again big media coverage, and then in the beginning of this year, spring this year. Those were the most important periods but it was quite high profile.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn now to RTL, the third major news programme, did you get provided information from their computer system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That was provided to you in the form of a computer printout from their archives?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That has been labelled as appendix 2, is that right, in relation to your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, your Honour, this has been provided to the Prosecution and I submit it for the Court as 101C.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 101C will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. [To the witness]: As with other documents, if we just flick through appendix 2, it frequently contains the name of Dusko Tadic and within each programme a summary of what the content of the programme was about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And also what kind of pictures were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. References to Omarska, Munich where the arrest took place, the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Interviews by Mr. Goldstone and other people from the Tribunal and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Chief Prosecutor of the Tribunal as well as mention of Radovan Karadzic, General Mladic. All within that context you will also find the reference to Dusko Tadic often in programmes of a wide concern as well as a specific concern ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- in relation to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps then if you can tell us what your findings were in relation to RTL?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right. So, altogether looking at their news programmes, Punkt Zwolf which is broadcasted at 12.00 a.m., then RTL Aktuell and Nachtjournal, they altogether had 20 reports mentioning at least the Tadic case, and 19 of them had one but most of them had different, even different, and more than one picture of Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just on that matter, were in fact pictures of this defendant emerging other than those taken at the time of his arrest by a television station, but pictures from his past emerging within programmes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I did not check exactly now on this RTL, but there were some pictures from Tadic as a younger man ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- from Bosnia doing some karate. That was very prominent as well, karate exercises, and with old friends. So they were not only from his arrest, and later in the day also from the Tribunal quite a lot of pictures ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- when he was arrested in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us then how many people watched RTL Aktuell in 1995, what their average viewing figure was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 3.5 -- 3.49 million people in the average, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us about the number of programmes that were played on RTL Aktuell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had seven programmes, or reports, about Tadic in RTL Aktuell, and in all of them they used photos of Tadic, different photos, and these were broadcasted again the same periods actually, in February 1994, on 14th and 15th, so two in February 1994, in November 1994, in April 1995, another one in April 1995, the first on 21st, the second on 24th, and even a third one on 26th April 1995 and May 1996. Again, RTL, the main show is at 6.45 p.m., and there are other RTL Aktuell shows during day time which use sometimes the same material.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So they recycle the material that may have been used on the main news slot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again do we see often a consistency within the dates by which this information is being put on the television stations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is quite open. Again after his arrest in February 1994, even two shows reports, then the first hearing of the Tribunal, November 1994, and then even three when in the period of his deferral to the Tribunal in April 1995 and the last one again in summer this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could you tell us about Nachtjournal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nachtjournal had nine reports about Tadic. Also, in all of them they used photos of Tadic and in the average, 1996, in October 1996, it is quite a new information, they had 1.16 million people watching Nachtjournal, and these reports were broadcasted again the same periods, in February 1994, in November 1994 twice or on two different days, on 7th and 8th, April 1995 on 21st, on 24th, on 26th, August 1995, March 1996 and May 1996, and the programme normally, on a normal day, is broadcasted twice at night at 0 a.m. and 3 a.m. in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Lastly, the other main news programme for RTL is Punkt Zwolf?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, which had four reports about the Tadic case and in three of them they used photos of Tadic and they were broadcasted again the same period, November 1994, April 1995, May 1996, these other three with photos of Tadic only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again information about average people watching, Punkt Zwolf on a day in October, it is 1.38 million people. It is only broadcasted once a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next television station that you were able to have access to, was that n-tv?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, n-tv, Der Nachrichtensender.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could say that a little bit slower because they have to put this on to the transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: N-tv, Der Nachrichtensender.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a German speaking all day news channel, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Having again access to their computer system, have you been able to compile that information on to an appendix 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, again this has been served on the Prosecution and I tender it as 101E, one for the Registry and three for your Honours. Your Honour, we have lost the transcript again this morning. It comes and goes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is particularly embarrassing for this to happen when Mr. Deichmann is here, considering the field you are in. It has never happened, Mr. Deichmann, with this frequency, I promise you!

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now I have it on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could tell us then about n-tv, what the product of your research was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did -- what they told me as a start, that it is an incomplete list which they could do. They were not able to do a complete list because it is a news all the day and they could not say how often it has been reported, different reports about the Tadic case. They found in a quick research in the period between October 1994 and May 1996 10 reports about the Tadic case. According to their own information, some of these reports have been shown 20 times, but they in the average calculate or they told me that one should calculate in the average that every report has at least been broadcasted eight times, and n-tv also was here in the spring this year live covering the Tribunal, I think, one or two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Their news channel has a major news slot at about every 30 minutes of the day, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In between that period are other features and other news analysis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on economy or some surveys.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Within your report you tell us that the reports were broadcasted in October 1994, November 1994, April 1995, three times in May 1996, although I can see five times in May 1996, judging by the dates. Is that a typographical error?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is three times on 7th May 1996, once on 8th May 1996, and then on 10th May 1996 another one, and on 12th and 13th May, so .....

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
