utterances.text: The viewing figures of that particular news channel, on average, each day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is 2.6 million people per day, which they calculate watch n-tv, an average time of 12 to 14 minutes. But, according to their own information, peaks reached the figure of even more than 3.5 million people watching it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As this is a rather slimmer document to the others that we have submitted, if we just look at the information which is very similar to the other archived material produced within appendix 2 and appendix 1, is it not ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- we can see here the date, would that be the date that this information was produced? 14.10 -- sorry, I am looking at the wrong part. Would that be the date that the information was on television, 14.10.1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I was as well for a while. I am looking at the first section on appendix 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I have to get the appendix out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The date that we see for that first passage on appendix 3, 14.10.1994, that would be the date of screening, would it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Below that at 10.7.24, that would be the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that is -- no, that is -- I actually do not know. I think it is some technical expression. The next one is about how long this report was. It is one minute 41 minutes -- so one minute 41 seconds, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. It gives a summary there of what would have been the subject matter ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- of the screening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is saying "Den Haag", The Hague, "Kriegsverbrechertribunal will Tadic", the War Crimes Tribunal wants Tadic, and the abstract is "Der in Munchen einsitzende Dusko Tadic soll vor UN-Kriegsverbrechertribunal in Den Haag".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could translate that for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Something like that, "In Munich, imprisoned Dusko Tadic is meant to be brought in front of the UN War Crimes Tribunal in The Hague".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It gives the sequences below, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. So that at the different sequences. So it is the first one is in Munich, a refugee home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume it is on interviews with refugees. Then it is a statement of a friend of Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then there are some pictures of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some pictures about torture, some dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then Netherlands, The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume the Court here, the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then it is Chief Prosecutor Richard Goldstone reading the indictment against Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. Again, this information is easily absorbed. If one goes through these passages, you can pick up the use of the information within each sequence and what the programme is about, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It shows the name of Tadic in virtually every programme. If we can now turn to the next matter which is SWF?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Kay, is there any objection to 101D?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. The next station with appendix 4 on your report is SWF, Suedwestfunk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, SWF, Suedwestfunk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could tell us about this particular television station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is one of the regional stations that were in all the Landers of Germany. They have regional stations, and that is in the south west of Germany, and it is broadcasted in co-operation with the first programme which I mentioned in the beginning, ARD. So it is actually the third channel, as we call it, ARD third channel. You can either reach it in the land you are living which is Baden-Wuerttemberg. You can also reach it via Astra satellite and you can reach it with Cable TV in three Laender in Germany, completely in Baden-Wuerttemberg, in Saarland and in Rheinland Pfalz.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: By "Laender", you mean districts of Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Areas of Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Then in the neighbouring parts of Baden Wurttemberg where this channel is based, in parts of the neighbouring Laender, you can reach it as well via Cable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So in Bavaria, in Hessen, in Nordrhein-Westfalen and in Sachsen Anhalt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again their computer was able to be accessed and material produced upon the number of programmes as well as their subject matter and the uses of the image of the defendant Tadic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is appendix 4, again served on the Prosecution. If I could submit this to the Registry as D101E? There are copies for your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 101E?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: SWF as a television channel is particularly important, is it not, in relation to Dusko Tadic, because a lady called Monika Gras did a number of documentaries about the issues concerning the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the former Yugoslavia ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- as well as concerning the defendant Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Her reports and documentaries were broadcasted on SW3 and also ARD, the first station we looked at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us, first of all, about the screening then of various documentaries, what they were called and the length of the films as well as the dates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right. One additional information, the third programmes, they have the Tagesschau, the news programme, which we talked about with ARD, they use the same material, but these are documentaries. So the first three documentaries that were produced, are actually a series, they are called Opfer des Krieges.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could just translate these as you go through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right. Victims of the war, No. 1, Kozarac ethnically cleansed, 84.09 minutes, was broadcasted on the 11th October 1993, by regional channel SW3, we just talked about. According to SWF information, Suedwestfunk information, 160,000 people watched this film altogether via satellite, via channel or via the normal procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The series that you spoke of was relayed the next night on 12th October ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a second part also entitled "Victims of the war, part 2", and the subtitle "Death camp Omarska"; the length 88.47 minutes, broadcasted one day after the first on 12th October 1993, again by SW3, and here Tadic is presented in a slow motion in Kozarac. So he was filmed by the crew already in spring 1993 when he was walking through the village wearing a leather jacket and a red shirt. This was even prior to his arrest, so October 1993. According to Suedwestfunk information, 250,000 people watched this film altogether -- "households", is a better expression, watched it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Then there was a third programme in this series, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was, as far as I remember, it was straight after this second ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- death camp Omarska report. That was actually an expert discussion where some journalists, some witnesses and other experts were discussing the matter of the Tribunal and war crimes in Bosnia. It was called "Victims of the war, No. 3, discussion", 63.15 minutes, the length, broadcasted on 12th October 1993 by SW3 and, according to SWF information, a few less people watched it. 100,000 people watched the discussion after the Omarska documentary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. The next programme, as a documentary rather than news programme, was shown on 14th February 1994, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, called "Blickpunkt Europa". That is a kind of a title for a programme which is broadcasted regularly but has different topics, though this was -- "blickpunkt" means something like "looking or spot Europe".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Spotlight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Spotlight Europe: the Tribunal", 44.05 minutes, the length, broadcasted on 14th February 1994 again by SW3, and I do not have any further information about how many people watched it. I could not deliver this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We just lost the transcript again, your Honour. The material in this film was very much the same material as that shown on another date in February 1994, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I have not seen this one, Blickpunkt Europa, personally but the title is the same, like others, number F, for example, and people who saw it told me that it was more or less the same material being used, also the date is actually the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not exactly the same day, but the next one was shown only a couple of days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. The programme then that used the same material was "War Criminals in Germany"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is even, this and the next one, the more important ones because they were produced by Suedwestfunk, but they were broadcasted by ARD which means all over Germany and also other in countries with a satellite or Cable TV could watch it. "Kriegsverbrecher in Deutschland", "War criminals in Germany", the tight, the subtitle, "The case Dule Tadic and of other Tatern, actors" or ......

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The length is 29.10 minutes broadcasted on 24th February 1994 which was very briefly after his arrest, broadcasted in ARD, and this video or this programme is quite a good example because there is actually Tadic shown in many different photos actually. More or less what existed at this time, photos of Tadic have been shown there and reproduced by other media. So it is again this image of Tadic in the leather jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You, in fact, list there six different types of photos that were used within the programme?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Bench can see the list there. We have no need to repeat them. What was the information, according to SWF, concerning the number of people watching this film?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1.96 million people, so nearly 2 million people or households were watching this documentary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. When you talk about satellite and these figures that we are given, it is common knowledge that you can pick up in other countries through other means, either by Cable or by satellite, the programmes in Germany, you can pick them up here in Holland, for instance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: ARD, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: ZDF?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: ZDF as well, the main channels, yes, RTL as well. So there are two satellite systems. One is Astra Satellite and another one is Yutel satellite which is European wide. I could look it up in what countries they are broadcasted, but ARD and ZDF is nearly everywhere in Europe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Can I ask, the numbers that are given, are they confined to Germany?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That was the next question, your Honour. I am grateful. I was going to ask that. The figures that we are given here, are they the whole of Europe or are they merely Germany?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is only Germany, but it includes, as I said, people who watch this documentary just via ARD with the normal procedure or via satellite or via Cable; but, altogether households watching in Germany, this particular documentary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Households in Holland, households in Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No idea. That is not included in these figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, and even in parts, Croatia, Austria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Austria, for definite, but these are also not included in these figures, but I am not sure if you can see it in Croatia, ARD, no idea. But these figures, as I said, are only for Germany, only for Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: If I can ask another question? Repeatedly it says "People"; is it people or households or television sets, in effect?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you help us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, that is my bad English, but it is households actually is the right word to mention here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So it is number of television sets on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As opposed to numbers watching the television set?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is information which is produced by companies who do some service for TV programmes because they want to know how many people watch it, and then they can sell their ads to other companies. So it is quite important for the prices you then, you know, make for advertisements and your programmes. So that is quite reliable sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, from your research, you are aware that these figures are figures that are important and figures that have to be produced carefully because ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- other commercial interests rely upon them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The programme at F, "The Tribunal"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was broadcasted as well in ARD, so the first main programme in Germany on 16th February 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The title is "The Tribunal: Victims, Prosecutors" -- no, "Taeter" means "actors" -- "Victims, actors prosecutors" ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Participants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Participants Judges. The War Crimes Tribunal", 61.01 minutes on 16th February 1995. This time much of the material was used from the Tribunal here. That was after the hearings had started already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And four times in this report Tadic photos were used twice. He is sitting in a car after his arrest in Munich wearing this sports training clothes and, according to Suedwestfunk, again 660,000 households in Germany watched this film. It was, I think, at 11 o'clock in the night, so it was quite late.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Have you put together a short video film of some 10 minutes relating to the material and images used within these documentaries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It is actually only from one documentary No. E, "Kriegsverbrecher in Deutschland", "War criminals in Germany", which we just talked about, broadcasted on 24th February 1994 with 1.96 million households watching it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The images of Tadic used within this programme, were they photographs that were picked up on and recycled throughout the news system? Were they the predominant source ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- of the image?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They are pictures from his arrest or even before his arrest when this camera team and photographer were looking where he was living, where Tadic is living, in Munich. Some of these photos, then films of his arrest in Munich, the photos of Kozarac, which I mentioned already, from spring 1993. Then also some pictures, older pictures, of Tadic doing karate exercises, being with friend in Bosnia. So I think that is quite a good summary of what has been reproduced as well by other papers or magazines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This has been put together into the form of a tape which we will now screen and has been handed to the technical booth, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So if we could put our video monitors on? Is it right that the sound will be switched off so we are not hearing the spoken word; we are going to be just looking at the film image?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is this going to be an Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, it is, your Honour, No. 102.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: We have never seen the video tape, your Honour. We just got a copy this morning as with the rest of this material, so I actually have no idea.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I have on my list of things to do to remind the Prosecutor to have translated the video that they offered when Mr. Ljubomir Tadic testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The problem being that they were just excerpts and they were in German. I gather this witness has put together highlights, as he sees them, from various films?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. He has used the image of Tadic which is the point of this evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is true, the image, but it is the frequency. It is excerpts from a number of films.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes -- from one film which was the predominant film.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry, OK. That makes the problem smaller then. Maybe we can then get the entire film and see it in context. I suppose that is the situation. It relates to the same offer that the Prosecution made regarding Ljubomir Tadic. We wanted to see it in context, see the entire film as well as see it in English or, at least, not in English, but at least the translation. So if you will do the same for this at least ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The Ljubomir tape Miss Hollis will be addressing after.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I can just stress here, your Honour, the point of this selection is the image rather than the programme itself or what was spoken.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will take a look at it and see how it fits in in perhaps the total film. Anyway, OK, you have not seen it, so we will take a look at it and then hear objections later, if there are any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think Mr. Deichmann wishes to assist us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I could make a brief comment about this? The question has just been raised; so this film was 29 minutes and it is in different periods where Tadic is being shown quite frequently. So it is after two minutes, the first time, and then after five minutes and half a minute and the second time. That is the first sequence we look at. Then it is actually 10 minutes where Tadic is not shown, but then from about a minute No. 15 to minute No. 22, we look at only one sequence which is complete without any cuts; whereas loads of material used, photos of Tadic. Then it is only one more which we will not see at minute 22, and then it is another seven minutes when the film was finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have we had cut out the 10 minutes bit without him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is cut out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is as I understood it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also the first five minutes is cut out and the last seven minutes is cut out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have a record there of what has been taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is helpful. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps now if the technical booth can put on our screens the film and lower the lights so we have a better image? (The video was played). Thank you, that is the film you put together, Mr. Deichmann. Amongst the photographs that we saw, there was the image of Mr. Tadic coming out of a house and dressed in a, I believe it is called, shell suit. We also saw another image of men in a bar or a room somewhere with copies of the same photograph and it being passed around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I am going to object to that question, your Honour. It calls for speculation. I certainly could not tell what that photograph was. I would like some voir dire from the witness whether he even knows before we have a conclusionary statement like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If I can assist the Court, because copies of the photographs from the film have been produced.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You are referring to when the men were looking at a piece of paper and there was a photograph on it ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- and that is what you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You can identify the image of Mr. Tadic in one of these photographs on the photograph being looked at by the men. If I refer my learned friend to the same scene and he looks at the photograph of the men with an ashtray in the foreground and looks at the photograph in the centre.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You two may be talking about something I do not understand. I thought the objection was to the portion of the film where people are looking at something, and it appears that included in what they are looking at is a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The question becomes, a photograph of whom? That is now what you are addressing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, your Honour, my objection was to the leading question which called for a speculative answer. Defence counsel is now referring to something they are apparently going to put into evidence which I would be happy for the Court to have because my objection still stands, as I do not believe you can tell. I simply wanted to know if this witness had any idea of what picture these people were looking and, if so, how does he know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall I ask that as a question then?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, since we have not been utilizing voir dire for the last six months, you might ask those questions so that we can determine whether there is this indicia of reliability.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As my learned friend has no objection to the photographs going in, perhaps I can produce them so they can be in front of your Honours as Exhibit 102B. If we call the video tape A. That is for the Registry which is the original photographs. These are photocopies for their Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The photo that Mr. Keegan was looking at was one of multiple people or is that not the one you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, there are actually two that are very similar.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What we have is a picture of one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: There are a whole sequence of photographs apparently here, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: May I apologise for the numbering because they were originally numbered for an entirely different purpose.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is OK. This is all 102B?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objection? 102B then will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The photograph we are concerned with would have "Tape 2, 21/27" on the left-hand side. Mr. Deichmann, have you got a copy of that photograph? You have only a photocopy ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a very bad photocopy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- I suspect. Let me give you mine or the Registry can provide you with it as they have finished noting it up. I believe there the bundle you have, which is the one filed with the Registry is, of original photographic images?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Actual photographs rather than what I have got which is a photocopy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think these are photographs done from the video tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I think Judge Stephen may have a similar set in his hand there.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: His are shiny!

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. The photograph that has got in the top left-hand corner "tape 2, 21/27", do you have any comments to make about that photograph in relation to what it represents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is a photo reproduced from the film we have just seen, which is the "War Criminals" broadcasted in ARD on 24th February 1994. It is about, after 18 minutes 25 seconds, Bosnian refugees in a pub with, I think it is quite clearly to see, blown up photos of Tadic. Actually in the middle of this photo you can see which here is No. 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see it from -- actually if you look from behind through it you can see that this one has written "troedel" marked on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are holding up to the Court now what has No. 2 on, although not No. 2 in the bundle, and it is a notice with "troedel" marked on it. The photograph that you are referring to, perhaps it could be put on the overhead monitor so you can point to the particular photograph and why you say these two are linked? I am afraid I wanted the one with "tape 2, 21/27" on the monitor. Which photograph do you say is linked to the photographs of Mr. Tadic, so that it is being looked at from the back? If you could just keep your thing on it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated] This one. I think that is the clearest expression of it, but I analysed the video quite carefully and also it is not as clear as here. It looks as though all the other pictures as well are blown up from this video ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- and distributed to Bosnian refugees. What you can see here, which is quite interesting as well, that is a sign which is in German pubs, this one here. It is on a different section of the video, much clearer, which is a sign which is in every pub for the protection of youth, saying that, you know, you should not give drinks to kids and so on. But it is in another aspect quite clear that is a German pub. I assume it is a pub in Munich. There is also a sign which says "Privat" private.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if we make no bones about it, what was the purpose of showing this bit of film within that documentary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the purpose, why was this being shown in the film about the war criminals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, the point which has been made not only in this documentary, is that many refugees recognised Tadic, so there are other bits in documentaries where witnesses who do not want to tell their names and so on confessed that they saw him, for example, in a shop in Munich and recognised him there. That was why just the sequences where they showed Bosnian refugees in Germany looking at it after his arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. That is all I ask about those particular photographs which we have produced as 102B. Thank you. One of the reasons for the interest within these German television programmes you have told us about is the European perspective, Germany being in the centre of Europe and the former Yugoslavia being a European country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Germany receive many people from the former Yugoslavia at the time of the conflicts in that country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have the exact figures here, but I would say now I am sure that it received the most refugees from all European countries. There are also loads in Austria, but in Germany there are, I do not know the figures, as I said, but the most of the refugees went to Germany. There is even now a big discussion about how they can be brought back securely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your research has been principally upon those television stations that we have covered in evidence this morning, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, also I did some more precise, I did some check-ups with them on the more precise journals for TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I just want to make it clear that you have not sought to produce before this Court all the television stations ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- within Germany or in Europe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But this has been an exercise focused upon that country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only on German, focused only on German, but on the most important news programmes and Suedwestfunk as an example because they produce these important documentaries which have been broadcasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Did you also consider special magazines for TV with political content?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I did as well. I looked, I tried to get information of special magazines or journals which are broadcasted, some of them weekly others monthly or fortnightly, and broadcasted either on private channels or on the main programmes in Germany. So I checked on Spiegel Teufel which is a TV programme but linked to a very prominent magazine, printed magazine, Der Spiegel. The same with Stern Teufel, a TV programme which belongs to ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, the transcript has gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am sorry. We are nearly making it to the end of the evidence. So Spiegel TV was a particular television journal with political content that you looked at, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That was actually the only one who told me that they had done a report about the Tadic case. All the others which I checked, the most important ones, the others did not do anything, but Spiegel TV is the third biggest political journal on TV. They have on average in 1994, that was when their report, one report was broadcasted, they had 3.93 million people watching to it, and this one report 10 minutes long was broadcasted on 3rd March 1994. Again, Tadic is shown there with an old karate friend, even some more details, information here. Once he is shown again in training clothes entering this house in Munich where he then was captured by the police. Then later in the film after three minutes he is shown doing karate exercises.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then after eight, nearly nine, minutes he is again showed with an old friend, Tadic wearing a beard. Actually, we have also some of these photos in this collection here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them also have been shown by the other film we just saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, on Judge Stephen's point, by 3.93 million people, do you mean households or individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Spiegel Teufel I would have to look up my figures if it is people or households.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say now, because some may differ. Some may even give you the breakdowns of the age of people. So I would have to check this. I am not sure now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you also review the German print media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you consider the biggest and most important German weekly magazine, I say that with deference to the others, but Der Spiegel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did they tell you the number of articles and photos that were used of the defendant Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we even produced an appendix for this as well, but they had ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if that could be produced now then as Appendix 5. This has been served on the Prosecution, your Honour. I produce this as 101F with a copy for the Registry and three for your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 101F will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Just for the record, there was apparently no ruling on my prior objection to the questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Well, I do not think Mr. Kay went back to the question, that I recall. I thought it had to do with who was in that photo that we saw. Was that your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We never got an answer from the witness that I heard. He did say that he looked at some blown up photos when he was looking at the video, but he never told us what was in it. I would like to blow up ours because it is difficult. Anyway, this 101F. If that is your objection -- if you want a ruling I will rule. I just maybe have lost the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I was just noting for the record that an objection had been made and there had been no answer to it. So it was just for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am quite happy with the way things have gone. I do not know whether Mr. Keegan is or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: To save confusion, your Honour, I will withdraw the objection. I will just handle it in cross.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will see. 101F then is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged. [To the witness]: If you tell us about -- not all of them are of war criminals either, the pictures here -- if we consider then your research from Der Spiegel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I said it is the most prominent or biggest weekly magazine or the biggest in circulation, but it is very well-known with a print run, I have a figure of the last quarter of 1995 with over a million, 1,033,344, quite an exact figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to a print run, that does not necessarily mean that that number of people look at a magazine. Could more people look at the same magazine if it arrives on a household doorstep?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, that is what some papers complain always about, that other people very often read these papers as well and they would prefer to sell it. I do not have the exact figures, but normally more people read these magazines than there were sold.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could tell us then about its reproduction of information concerning Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: OK. They had four articles from the beginning of 1994 to the middle of 1996, and in these four articles all four of them included photos, altogether five photos. One article had even two photos of Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the periods I only have the number of the week, number 8, 1994, for example, you if you look at No. 8 it means it is the eighth week of the year which will be around February 1994, which means after his arrest in Munich. Two photos of Tadic, one with a glass of wine and another one doing karate exercises. The next article from Spiegel No. 45, 1994, again a photo of Tadic, actually the same photo of Tadic like the other one with a glass of wine. This is around week 45 in this year, which is around November.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume at the time when the Tribunal hearings started. The third one, No. C, is No. 18, 1995, Spiegel issue, one photo of Tadic, him doing karate exercises. This would be around April/May, so the time of his deferral to the Tribunal from Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The last one, No. D, issue of Spiegel No. 29, 1996, a photo of Tadic here in front of the Tribunal, in front of the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you also do the same exercise in relation to Fokus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The magazine that you classify as being the second most important after Der Spiegel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a news magazine, yes, Spiegel is the most important news magazine. Fokus is quite a new one. It does not exist for such a long time as Spiegel, but it has become quite important as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to this, did you also access their records and did they produce a summary of the information that you have in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is Appendix 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Appendix 6. I put this in for completeness because you actually set it out within the report. Your Honour, if this could be submitted by the Defence as 101G. A copy has already been served on my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 101G?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Does that relate to Appendix 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is Appendix 6, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In fact, your report in English sets out this information in the form of a summary, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could tell us then about the articles run by Fokus during that same period, from February 1994 until October 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So it was actually between February 1994 and the last one was in April 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first one -- altogether, the summary of this research, they had eight articles concerning the Tadic case in this period, and in four of them they had three photos and one caricature. So three photos I think that is the most important.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: By "caricature" you mean cartoon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A cartoon, yes. So the first one on 21st February 1994, one article where there is a photo of Tadic which was reproduced quite often in a car after his arrest in Munich wearing his training clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The second one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second one an article on 2nd May 1994 about the work of the Tribunal but no photo of Tadic, just been mentioned. The third one is what I referred to already, the cartoon which was printed in the issue of 14th November 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then now No. 40D in my report, this is an article printed on 29th April 1995, again no photo. Then E an article printed on 12th June 1995, again no photo. F an article on 23rd October 1995 where you see a photo of Tadic at the Tribunal. Then again an article without a photo printed on 17th February 1996. The last one on 29th April 1996, again with a photo of Tadic at the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The print run of Fokus in the last quarter of 1995, did that average to being slightly over 750,000?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, 751,714.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, with the same proviso that more people often read magazines than ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- are actually sold to individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also I cannot give a figure on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. To round up this now with Stern magazine, another popular weekly magazine, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is a very popular weekly magazine. Also a kind of news magazine but more popular. It even has a higher print run than Spiegel has. So the print run in the last quarter of 1995, the same period as the other papers I just talked about, was 1,251,038. So they had in the period also between beginning of 1994 and mid-1996, altogether they had seven articles concerning the Tadic case and five of these seven articles included altogether six photos of Tadic. So, to go through in more detail, the first appeared in Stern No. 9, 1994 which is again the week No. 9, February 1994 I would assume or the beginning of March after his arrest, with two photos of Tadic in a car, again after his arrest in Munich, and the other one Tadic doing karate exercises.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: B Stern No. 26, 1994 which would be around April/May, one article with one photo of Tadic again in a car after his arrest in Munich. No. C, Stern No. 45, 1994, again a photo of Tadic in a car after his arrest in Munich.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. D Stern No. 24, 1995, a photo of Tadic at the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So, the one before No. 45, 1995, is around the time of November when the hearings started here. The one I just talked about No. D24, 1995, that would be the middle of 1995, the time around when he was deferred. Then No. E, an article in Stern No. 6, 1996, which is in February 1996, no photo of Tadic. Another article just three weeks later which is March 1996 Stern No. 9, 1996, without a photo. The last one No. 20, 1996 and the time of April 1996, I assume, a photo of Tadic at the Tribunal going with this article. That is it, seven articles, five of them, six photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour that is a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess until 2.30.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Mr. Deichmann, over the lunch adjournment did you make some enquiries over the matter of people and households which was a concern of the Judges? Can you tell us what the result of those enquiries were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did some brief enquiries and when we discussed this with Suedwestfunk, which is No. 5 in my report, I got confused looking at the numbers of households, being satellite and so on. Actually, the question your Honour asked about if it is people or households when we talked about this important report, "War Criminals in Germany", which was broadcasted in February 1994, on 24th, we saw bits of it, I mentioned the figure 1.96 million people and actually what is in the report is correct. It is not households, it is people. I checked this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Deichmann. If we could next turn to the Sueddeutsche Zeitung which is the German daily paper with the highest circulation? As a result of enquiries from their computer system, did you have provided for you a computer printout which is appendix 7 concerning the number of articles they have printed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again, your Honour, this has been served on the Prosecution and I produce it now as Exhibit 101I. There are three copies for your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I wonder if I can just clarify one aspect of it? Apart from that one instance, other references to "people" are to television sets, are they, or throughout your report where you mention "people", does it mean people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It means people, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Not households?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Just to explain it, I got confused as well because they changed the system how they count a couple of months ago which has just been explained to me as well by these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This printout here is a summary of the articles on the Tadic case that were printed between February 1994 and October 1996, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The information about how many of these articles had photos of Tadic was not something that you were able to have provided to you during the period of time that your research was undertaken, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That has not been something you have been able to update since yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This particular newspaper, are you able to say whether photographs of Tadic were ever printed at all during the period of February 1994 and October 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, altogether they had (which is also down here) 82 articles which are listed on here covering the Tadic case, and for the print run is 402,608 which makes Sueddeutsche Zeitung the biggest paper in Germany. On the photos I cannot give any exact figures but, from my experience, I would guess there were quite a lot of pictures going with them, and actually maybe we can show this later, all the stuff that has been already distributed. If you take a look through this big file of collections of articles, there are loads of photos in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much. If we go to other sources and, indeed, you have referred to a ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Before we move on, are you just moving off this Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK, it is just that it has not been tendered yet that I am aware of and, before we do, I am a bit confused as to -- that is annex 7? That actually was not shown what was presented, annex 7?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What paragraph in the report are we referring to now? We seem to have jumped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Paragraph 4, after the "Stern" section.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to 101? It will be H.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: H, not I.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We are almost getting there and I may have slipped up on the procedures.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. You have referred to other sources which is on the next page of your report and a ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- that is quite all right --- and a bundle of newspaper cuttings for that period from February 1994 to October 1996. Can you tell us about this further bundle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is a bundle of articles collected from six important daily or weekly papers or magazines, which is the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, FAZ, with a print run of 390,586 ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- in the last quarter of 1995. It is Die Tageszeitung, TAZ, with a print run of 59,182. It is the Frankfurter Rundschau, FR, with a print run of 186,694. It is Die Zeit which is a weekly paper with a print run of 478,961, all in the last quarter of 1995. Then it is Der Spiegel we already talked about and Die Woche where I do not have the print run figure now, but these were looked quite consistently. It is not complete, but it is based on actually my own archives which I collected in the last couple of years and the archives of Mr. Heitmann. Altogether he put together in his document 83 articles from the period February 1994 to October 1996 concerning the Tadic case, and he found in 12 of these articles, 13 photos and two carricatures which are cartoons again. An important fact maybe is that only the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, FAZ, was the only daily or paper he looked at and I mentioned which did not have a photo with Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the others at least had one photo in these articles of Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: These research materials have been put together in a further bundle, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A copy of this has again been served on the Prosecution, your Honour, and we tender it now before the Court as 101. I have lost track now -- and three copies for your Honours?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 101I?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That will be admitted. The film that we saw was ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Was that 102?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you wish to offer that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 102? That has not been admitted, has it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. 102 then will be admitted, and 101I.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think you have adequately described this material, as a flick through of the contents shows the newspaper cuttings as well as the various photographs that have been used. Did you make enquiries of the GAFF photoagency in Berlin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could tell us what that particular agency does as a service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I did this research on the Suedwestfunkt and these films produced there, the GAFF or GAFF photoagency was mentioned as having the copyrights for actually all the photos that were taken of Dusko Tadic before his arrest in Munich, and so I got in contact with them -- they are based in Berlin -- and I talked to the photographer who took the photos. According to his information, he could not give me exact figures, but he was saying that after Tadic's arrest in Munich in February 1994 that all important newspapers immediately bought the pictures and published them, which actually confirms the other research we already talked about. So he mentioned Die Zeit, Frankfurter Rundschau, Stern, Spiegel, Fokus, and papers which have not been mentioned as a weekly called Freitag and another daily, small daily paper, with a print run of 20,000 called Junge Welt. So, these one, two -- seven papers he mentioned having in mind that they bought his photos with Tadic before the arrest. He also told me that they have been printed very often in Germany, and that there is another international photoagency in Paris called SIPA Press which actually sold these photos a lot of time worldwide.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. These agencies are used as distribution centres by newspapers who call up the material and then buy the rights and have them put in their own newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In addition to that research within Germany, did you also contact a Mr. Philip Hammond from Great Britain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is he a media specialist at the University of North London?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no idea if he is at the University of North London, but I know him through the London International Research Exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he again provide information concerning a check on some of the archives of various British newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he also advise you from his research of the information that was able to be obtained from the newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To bear in mind as well what he told me is that that is an incomplete list. But what he did, he looked at altogether 13 different papers where, from my knowledge, 12 of them are British and I think the only one, Newsweek, I think, is published in America, an American weekly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But they are read also in Europe and in Britain, in particular. So, 13 different papers and he found 52 articles were concerning the Tadic case. Then in terms of photos in these 52 articles, in 22 articles photos of Tadic appeared. There was only one paper which did not run a photo of Tadic which is, if you can see in the list, The Observer, where he found one article but not a single photo. Then should I go through this list as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. What did The Guardian produce?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He found 18 articles of The Guardian and four photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A readership of a quarter of a million?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, according to his information, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Daily Telegraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He found eight articles and in five of them photos of Tadic, and a readership of estimated a million.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Times, six articles, one photo in these and a readership of estimated 400,000.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Independent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Independent, five articles, four photos of Tadic and a readership estimate of 250,000.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Financial Times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Financial Times, four articles, one photo of Tadic, altogether a readership of 240,000 where he gave me additional information that about 50 per cent, though 120,000 are sold in Britain and the rest abroad. So that is international figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The European?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three articles, one photo in these, no idea about the readership.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Daily Mail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two articles, one photo and a readership of more than a million.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Newsweek?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Newsweek is, I think, an American magazine, weekly, with one article and going along with a photo of Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Sunday Times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Sunday Times, he found one article going along with a photo of Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Observer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I mentioned already, the only paper with no photo of Tadic, one article, no photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Evening Standard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Evening Standard, one article with one photo of Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Economist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same, one article, one photo of Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Daily Express?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again one article, one photo of Tadic and a readership estimated more than a million.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again that is all I ask, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Deichmann, can you explain to the Court, with reference to the television markets that you discussed earlier, what is "market share"? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is -- I just have to get the figures out again -- what it means, if you take all television consumers as 100 per cent, then 16 of them or 16.8 per cent, which you could not calculate, would look RTL regular ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, I understand the figures. What I want to know is what does the term "market share" mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Germany, it means "markt anteiler" which means how important this television programme is on a national area in terms of being shown by people -- watched by people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know how the television networks determine the figures then that they have given you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually, these information are, as I said, already not given, but I could look it up very explicitly where I got these figures from, but these figures are provided by, as I said, some companies, independent companies, which are recognised actually by all the media companies for these advertisement business jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What I want to know is, do you know how they get those figures, what exactly do they do to come up with 16.8 per cent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I was alluding to when I talked about households and people watching it. They do -- how do you call it in English -- a kind of survey. They look at a certain number of people and take this as an average, but it is -- actually these figures are agreed on by all the major, actually by everybody. Everybody is working after them. I could ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So, as far as you know, these are based on surveys of the consumers; they call people or write them and ask them, "What did you watch? What do you watch?" How do they do this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no information how they get it together. It is done by the Gesellschaft fur Konsumerforschung in Nuremberg, GFK, which, I think, even got an official order by all these companies -- by all the TV channels to provide this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: As far as you are aware, the purposes of this is for them to be able to determine their market share so that they know how much they can charge for the advertising time they sell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that is one important aspect, but I am not sure if it is actually -- I am sure it is also of purpose for other -- important for other purposes, but that is what I know, where it is used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you know or are you aware of any studies with respect to how people who do not speak the language German in Germany and who are at the bottom of the ethnic scale, the most disadvantaged, how they fit into this equation of market share? Are they a disproportionately high percentage of the 20 per cent who are not even represented within your figures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Are you aware of any studies with respect to this issue of market share that specifically consider people who do not speak the German language ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: --- or are the most economically disadvantaged within the German society ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: --- and whether or not they make up a disproportionately high share of the 20 per cent of market share who, apparently, do not even fit into the numbers that you give us here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have no information. I could only guess that, or some information here, that I think about more than 80 per cent of all households in Germany have access to a television, or I think it is even more. I think there were some on cable or so, but I have no concrete or definite information about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: All the articles which you have produced here today are in the German language, are they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Besides the last ones about the British which I just discussed at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You actually have not produced any of those articles, have you? I am talking about the Exhibits here in Court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean about printed articles? I refer here in Der Spiegel, no, I have never written for Der Spiegel, never for the Fokus, Stern, Sueddeutsche Zeitung, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I will move on, sir, thank you. Do you know any of the witnesses in the Tadic case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You have never met any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I do not know who the witnesses are. I only know ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So you have no idea how many of them speak German?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you have any idea of how many of those witnesses may have televisions? Do you know how many of those people have ever read a German newspaper or a German magazine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no concrete information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You would not have any information then on how many may have satellite TV or Cable TV either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. But just, in general, most of the households in Germany have televisions. It is very rare to find houses that do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Really? Would it surprise you to find out that almost 5 million households do not have television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: It would not surprise you? In your report you refer to several factors that were of particular interest to German society ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: --- with respect to this whole issue. Is it not a fact that you yourself have had a very keen interest in the media coverage of this particular conflict for the last few years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had a particular interest, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In fact, I believe you testified earlier that you have collected your own archives ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: --- including going to three to four daily newspapers as well as the weeklies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but that is to explain, as a freelancer, quite a normal procedure you have to do, because I do not have access to AP or DPA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In fact, your focus, though, with respect to the coverage of this conflict is that you are very critical of the way the media has covered this conflict, are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I did not only collect articles in my archives about the media, I actually collected nearly everything I could find, and then for this report here I took out everything I could find about the Tadic case. So it is actually only a selection of what I have been collecting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not only mine. It is, as I referred to, also from Mr. Heitmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes. My question to you was that your focus with respect to the media coverage in your writings is to be very critical of the way the media has covered this conflict and, in fact, you accuse it of being anti-Serb, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have been -- again could you repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: I will break it down for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your focus has been to be critical of the way the media has covered this conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In fact, you have accused it of being anti-Serb and being an instrument of western governments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have been quite critical and for criticising them for being one-sided, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Sir, do you think that your extreme personal interest in the media coverage of this conflict might affect the objectivity of your conclusions in your report as to whether the average media viewer might have seen the coverage of the Tadic case?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry, your Honour. I think my learned friend is making a comment in the question there which, in the circumstances, is not called for. There is no evidence that it is an extreme personal interest that this expert has before the Court. He has only come here to produce figures concerning viewing and article circulation. To be frank, I do not see what the point is in putting the question that way.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is cross-examination. It is, you know, his definition of "extreme"; if he feels it is not, he can say "no".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will overrule your objection. You need to answer the question. Maybe it needs to be repeated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat it? I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Certainly. (To the witness): My question was whether or not you would agree that your very strong personal interest in the media coverage of this conflict might affect your objectivity when you reached your conclusions with respect to whether or not the average media consumer would have seen the coverage of the Tadic case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think, no, I do not have a personal interest. I have an interest as a journalist and that is what I was looking at and why I was looking at. There is no personal interest involved in this area. As I explained also I did some other areas I looked at. So I criticised the media also for other things. We did this project about D Day, for example, about images of Japan, and I think that is what my figures show. There is no subjectivity in it. I wanted to present objective facts. There is no personal interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If we could go to some of these factors then. It might be easier to start from the last, perhaps that is most recent in your mind. First of all, as I read your report, a colleague in Britain actually did the review of these newspapers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You yourself, in fact, did not do this review and so you cannot vouch for its accuracy, can you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What he emailed me is not these figures, but he emailed me a list of the titles which I have here as well, the authors, also a short abstract of all the articles and also explaining what photos were used. I did actually count them and I calculated these figures together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you review each one of these articles completely yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, just as I described what I got from him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So let us go to next series that you received from a colleague, and that would be under paragraph 5 "Other Sources" which has been produced to this Court. You indicated that those documents were looked at quite consistently by you and your colleague, you referred him to some of them, and that it is a compilation of 83 articles concerning the Tadic case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is actually what you have as a copy of this file here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Are you aware then that at least 10 of these articles do not mention Tadic at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not aware of this, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be a surprise for me actually, but this was done by Mr. Heitmann this summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In fact, you included some of your own articles and your colleague's articles on the critical coverage of the media in this conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Of these 83 you indicate that 12 I believe ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: --- or as I look through them 12, yes, 12 carry photos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you have any idea whether any of the witnesses in this case saw any of those 12 photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If we then go to the list from the ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sueddeutsche Zeitung.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, the research service. That was paragraph 4 which I missed originally. You indicated again that this was 82 articles about the Tadic case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not about it all in particular, but at least mentioning Tadic. They have a research system where you give them a name and then they find it on their system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Because we only have the titles here. So it is quite conceivable then, for example, that the article which is entitled Louise Arbour, the Chief Prosecutor Tribunal in The Hague, may mention the word "Tadic"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And that suffices for your research?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and there is also no information about photos here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: With respect to these broadcasts, for example, the RTL broadcast, these extracts indicate of the 20 broadcasts which mention Tadic 15 indicate that a picture of Tadic was actually shown?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Which one is this? I am sorry, Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That would be No. 2, your Honour, the RTL, the second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is No. 3 RTL.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You are correct, the annex.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Annex 2, Appendix 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That is what I was thinking of, 2. In these stories then which actually show a picture of Mr. Tadic, the complete stories themselves range from 11 seconds to five minutes. You have no indication in here of how long the picture of Mr. Tadic may have actually been on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Well, that is a news programme, so I think it would be like in an average news programme also here or in Britain, just a couple of sentences I would guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That would hold true for all of the broadcasts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That would hold true then for all of the broadcasts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of the news which I mentioned, yes, like Heute or ARD before, yes, like normal news or sometimes they have it as a background when the speaker is on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: With ARD, for example, it would be anywhere from 31 seconds to three minutes per story?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is very rare that you have longer things in the main news. Three minutes is actually very long in the main news.
