utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: With respect to the video that you showed, it was my understanding that those were segments of photographs of the accused, and yet I saw several sequences of a man in a profile, a darkened profile. Do you have any idea who that man was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was mentioned as a lawyer in Hamburg who was, I do not know now, but I think he was presenting one of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The man with a beard that was shown with the glasses, who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite at the end was he? Yes, I think it is was a psychologist or some person from Bosnia, but I do not remember his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your testimony with respect to the group of people that were looking at a photograph, you indicated that you thought it might be a bar in Munich?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And you thought that they were Bosnian refugees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was that information that you obtained from watching the video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is mentioned in the video itself "Bosnian refugees", but about Munich that was actually what I guessed because in an earlier stage in this video there is somebody interviewed in this pub, another person, and the way he talks in one second he gave the impression because he mentions Munich at first. So that is why I thought that it is in Munich, but it could have been another German pub as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You actually have no idea who those people in the photograph are, in the video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the video we saw I do not have any idea, no. The person who has been interviewed before is mentioned with a name but we did not see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. Once again, with respect to that particular video, the figure of 1.96 million, do you know how they actually derived that figure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is the same as I explained before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just on one of the last matters that you were referred to about the video and the clip in the video concerning the men looking at pictures as you surmised being in a bar, did the video say that they were looking at pictures of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no, it did not say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The connection with Tadic comes from the photographs we looked at and the image that we had earlier on in the sequence with that notice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and also the story of the whole report. It would make sense in the story as well, quite a logical step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are a freelance journalist, as you told us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As a freelance journalist in your own personal capacity you provide articles from either the mainstream perspective or contrary to the mainstream perspective?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I am doing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mainly contrary to the mainstream perspective.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, but as far as your research for the Defence is concerned, whatever you may have written, that was unimportant in relation to the figures that you produced to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what I think is completely unimportant. That is very objectively done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were asked about television in Germany. Is Germany a country where they have bars with televisions on the walls or on the counters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In some, but there are other countries I remember from holidays where there are more televisions, but I could not guess. There are some, yes, where people meet and watch news or watch football or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Nothing, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Mr. Deichmann being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Mr. Deichmann, you are permanently excused. That means you are free to leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: On Tuesday we will begin at 9 o'clock, if that is acceptable with you lawyers, and we will adjourn at 3.30. I wanted to tell you that basically just using the time while Mr. Deichmann is gathering his material. Mr. Deichmann, the next time you return, if you ever do, I promise that the transcript is going to be working absolutely 100 per cent! So 9 o'clock on Tuesday I wanted to tell you that and we will adjourn at 3.30. Mr. Kay, would you call your next witness or Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We have concluded by the evidence we presented to you our case. We rest our case, with the proviso, your Honour, that we are investigating matters related to Witness L, and if that might result in anything we think your Court should be informed of, we will tell you about that and we may tell you how we would find that the case would proceed. So far we rest our case here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you. Miss Hollis, I mentioned the video involving Mr. Ljubomir Tadic. Do you rise to tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, I do. Your Honour, as you recall that was marked as Prosecution Exhibit 360 for identification. As you recall, that was two short film clips, one showing Mr. Ljubomir Tadic in the cafe in Kozarac, the other showing him at the monument. Following the issues of translation that arose in the courtroom, we re-contacted Spiegel TV and they were this time able to provide us with the original film footage before it had been voice-overed in German. So what we have done to ensure that those two clips are complete, is we have now a new video segment. This video segment has, first, what you saw before, the German voice-over version, followed by that same footage but in the original Serbo-Croatian. What we have done to assist you with the translation of those segments is that we have had the German voice-over translated in so far as the German commentary to put the context in. Then we have had the original Serbo-Croatian translated so that you have Mr. Tadic's own words in his own language to you. To clarify the record, what I would like to do, I did not offer Prosecution Exhibit 360, I would like to withdraw that. I would like to offer this new composite film clip that we have provided that I just told you about, that would be Prosecution Exhibit 362A for identification, and this new translation as Prosecution Exhibit 362B for identification. We have previously provided the Defence with both a copy of this new film clip and also with a copy of this new translation. I think that should address the concerns about completeness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, is there any objection to Prosecution 362A and B?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour. We have come to an agreement on this point.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. They will be admitted. 360 was not admitted?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: In any case, it is withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I have provided copies of the translation for the Court and, as I indicated, I have previously provided that to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The other matter I had a note to myself about was the military book of Witness W. Have you been able to speak with Mladen Tadic to find out where it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have no positive results to report to the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that still a request, the military book, for Witness W?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We would like to continue that request.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You have been unable to locate Witness W, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We have no report of people who have spoken to him who could tell me where he is and whether he is willing to hand over that document.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So you have been unable to locate him?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there anything else we need to consider at this time? Otherwise the Prosecution will begin its rebuttal Tuesday at 9 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. The Court is adjourned until Tuesday at 9 a.m. (3.25 p.m.).

procedural_notes.text: (The Court adjourned for a short time)
